summary:
After a bad night, sleeping in can feel like the obvious fix. But the pressure to sleep builds from the moment you get up, so a sleep-in can leave less of it at bedtime.

In this article, psychologist Matthew Hallam explains sleep drive, why getting up at your usual time after a poor night matters, and when a modest catch-up on days off may still make sense.

Equal Psychology provides psychological support for adults with sleep difficulties in Kew, Croydon, and online across Melbourne.

Medicare rebates available with a GP referral.
